data.narrative: Completed Module 4 'Vertical Slicing' learning about breaking work into thin end-to-end slices, distinguishing horizontal layers from vertical slices, writing explicit anti-scope to prevent scope creep, and using human-testable acceptance criteria.

dimension_scores.observation: Defined 6 vertical slices (including payment spike) with explicit scope, anti-scope, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and complexity estimates
dimension_scores.evidence: artifacts/vertical-slices-module-04.md contains 6 slices with detailed scope and anti-scope

dimension_scores.observation: Slices build on each other - Slice 1 has no dependencies, Slice 2 depends on Slice 1, Slice 3 depends on Slices 1 and 2, showing logical progression
dimension_scores.evidence: Slice definitions explicitly state dependencies (e.g., 'Slice 2 depends on Slice 1 - builds on booking data model')

dimension_scores.observation: Chose demand side first to test core value proposition immediately, avoiding supply-side risk of building provider registration without knowing if users want to book
dimension_scores.evidence: module4_context.md explains demand side first tests whether users complete booking flow, which is the biggest product risk

dimension_scores.observation: Each slice has specific scope, detailed anti-scope (10+ items for Slice 1), and human-testable acceptance criteria (no 'check database' steps)
dimension_scores.evidence: Anti-scope explicitly lists excluded items like 'No user authentication', 'No payment processing', 'No email or push notifications'

dimension_scores.observation: Responded to stakeholder pressure to add payments by creating Slice 1.5 payment spike instead of expanding Slice 1, preserving thin first slice while meeting investor need
dimension_scores.evidence: module4_break.md and updated slices show payment spike added as standalone slice, keeping Slice 1 thin for clean learning

dimension_scores.observation: Distinguished horizontal layers (data, backend, UI) from vertical slices (feature threads), ensuring each slice is end-to-end and testable through UI
dimension_scores.evidence: module4_context.md identifies horizontal layers (data storage, backend logic, user interface) and defines minimal vertical slice that goes end-to-end

strengths: Defined 6 vertical slices with explicit anti-scope preventing scope creep
Chose demand side first to test core value proposition immediately
Added payment spike slice to address investor pressure while preserving thin first slice
Human-testable acceptance criteria for all slices (no technical verification steps)
data.recommendation: Use vertical slices as foundation for Module 5 Ticket Writing - decompose each slice into specific tasks with acceptance criteria that another developer or AI agent can execute

public_evidence.student_action: Defined 6 vertical slices for SkillSwap including payment spike (Slice 1.5) to address investor pressure while preserving thin first slice, each with explicit scope, anti-scope, dependencies, and human-testable acceptance criteria
public_evidence.technical_detail: Slices: 1 Browse/Book (2-3 hours), 1.5 Payment Spike (2-3 hours), 2 Auth (1-2 days), 3 Provider Self-Service (1-2 days), 4 Payment Processing (2-3 days), 5 Real-Time Availability (3-4 days). Anti-scope explicitly lists 10+ excluded items per slice.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Demonstrates ability to break complex features into thin, end-to-end slices that are buildable, testable, and can be demonstrated to stakeholders while managing scope creep

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Defined horizontal layers (data, backend, UI) and created minimal vertical slice that goes end-to-end from database to UI
Each slice has explicit anti-scope listing 10+ excluded items to prevent scope creep and stakeholder confusion
Added Slice 1.5 payment spike to address investor need without expanding Slice 1, preserving thin first slice

learning_style_signals: prefers concrete examples and stakeholder scenarios
